sources.claim: Logging filters select entries within the chosen resource scope; resource fields and absolute timestamp comparisons can bound an incident search.
logging read supports explicit project, order and limit; freshness applies only to descending reads without timestamp filters.
LogEntry timestamp is the event time and receiveTimestamp is when Cloud Logging received the entry; those times can differ.

a.conclusion: The saved empty search covered the stage project, us-east1 and the previous hour, not the intended prod/us-central1 incident. A correctly scoped saved read found both events already ingested. This explains the empty search, not the acknowledgement failures.
next_checks: Compare the saved scope with the intended project, resource labels and absolute event-time window; retain bounded result coverage.
Morgan asks the application/dependency owner for timings correlated to audit-0310 and audit-0720.
Use the available canonical bounded logging read and distinguish its supplied records from live execution.
unsupported: Logging permissions or delayed ingestion caused this particular empty result.
Zero rows prove successful acknowledgements or service recovery.
A broader role, unbounded search or logging configuration change is required.
unknowns: The mechanism of the acknowledgement failures.
Whether users recovered after the supplied incident window.

b.conclusion: The first query matched the intended scope, but both events arrived at 14:15:04, after its 14:11 execution. The same query later found them. The empty result reflects delayed log availability, not a healthy zero or a scope error.
next_checks: Compare timestamp and receiveTimestamp against the read execution time and declared event coverage.

unknowns: Why the client batch remained queued.
